_why: One deliberate behavioural change per lane, applied to z47's own Zig owner, that the lane MUST detect. A mutant that survives is a hole in the lane, not a bug in the owner. Never mutate the imported c43 tree: it is the reference, and editing it inverts what the lane measures.
_how: check-oracle-negative-control.py applies each `find` -> `replace` (which must match exactly once), rebuilds and runs `step`, requires a non-zero exit, then restores the file. A mutant that fails to COMPILE counts as killed: the lane refused the change.
_survivors: A survivor that is genuinely equivalent to the original gets `expected_survivor` with the reason and stops failing the gate. A survivor without one fails it. Do not delete an entry to make this pass.

mutants.what: real34IsNegative stops being a raw sign-bit test
mutants.why: realType.h:105 is the sign bit; decQuadIsNegative excludes zeros and NaNs, so -0 answers differently. The signed-zero predicates must catch this.

mutants.what: fnGetType divides by 100 instead of 1000
mutants.why: The type report's scale. A lane that does not compare the produced value would miss it entirely.

mutants.what: swapRealImaginary zeroes the bytes instead of writing decQuad's zero
mutants.why: Sixteen zero bytes is a different member of zero's cohort. Only a byte-level comparison of the register payload sees it.

mutants.what: conjCxma stops restoring a positive sign on a zero imaginary part
mutants.why: Guards the complex-matrix branch, which no fixture in any lane reached until seedComplexMatrix existed. It needs BOTH halves of the condition arranged -- a zero imaginary part and SPCRES clear -- and this mutant survived until seedComplexMatrixImagZero cleared the flag, because the harness leaves it at its reset value of SET.

mutants.what: the lettered reserved variables stop owning a null payload pointer
mutants.find: const C47_NULL: u16 = 65535; // defines.h: the null register-data pointer
mutants.replace: const C47_NULL: u16 = 0; // defines.h: the null register-data pointer
mutants.why: registers.c reads C47_NULL as `this entry owns no payload`; 0 makes every lettered reserved variable look writable. This is the defect the lane was built to find.

mutants.what: liftStack shifts one register too few
mutants.why: The stack lift is the operation this lane exists to compare; stopping at Y leaves X holding the wrong value.

mutants.what: the RXFN section marker is misspelled on the way out
mutants.why: The .sav/.d47 writer's section tag for full-precision XFN registers, reached through the data-file export the lane now drives.

mutants.what: a user flag resolves to the wrong bank word
mutants.why: Flag-to-bit resolution is the whole subject of this lane.

mutants.what: the shift result skips the word-size mask
mutants.why: Every shift result is masked to the word size; dropping it leaks bits above it.

mutants.what: NOT stops masking to the word size
mutants.why: NOT is the only one of the seven logical ops c43's corpus exercises at a word size below 64 (not.txt has WS=13 as well as WS=64). At WS=64 the mask is all-ones and dropping it is an EQUIVALENT mutant -- which is what the first attempt here picked, on NAND, and why it survived. The corpus is the oracle and is never extended, so NOT is where this behaviour is reachable.

mutants.what: a tone plays the wrong frequency
mutants.why: The frequency table is what this lane compares.

mutants.what: an allocation stops updating the used-block count
mutants.why: The pool's used-block accounting is what this lane diffs against c43's.

mutants.find:

    if (number_of_bits > runtime.shortIntegerWordSize) {
mutants.replace:
pub export fn fnMaskl(number_of_bits: u16) callconv(.c) void {
    if (number_of_bits > runtime.shortIntegerWordSize + 1) {
mutants.why: The word-size bound on MASKL. The first attempt here mutated rotate_bits, which this lane does not drive at all -- it drives the bit-manipulation commands (Bc/Bs/Cb/CountBits/Fb/Maskl/Maskr/Sb).

mutants.what: ln(0) stops returning -infinity
mutants.why: The zero-argument branch of the complex logarithm, which this oracle drives directly.

mutants.what: no single owner behaviour to mutate
mutants.no_mutation: This lane compares STRUCT LAYOUTS against translate-c'd upstream headers, so the only mutation it can detect is a layout change -- and any layout change breaks every other lane first, which makes it a mutation of the whole tree rather than of this one. Its negative control is that it caught real layout drift when it was written. Recorded rather than forced.

mutants.what: no single owner behaviour to mutate
mutants.no_mutation: This lane proves every migrated sprintf->std.fmt translation is byte-identical to libc's. A mutation of the Zig side is exactly what it is built to catch, so it is already its own negative control: the lane exists because the translation could differ. A separate mutant would restate the lane.

mutants.what: changeSign stops routing a time register to its own worker
mutants.why: The lane that is the ONLY coverage for 86 of 120 math wrappers had no mutant at all. changeSign.c dispatches dtTime before the monadic table and the driver seeds two time fixtures, so the branch is reachable and observable in the snapshot.

mutants.what: glyphLength counts a two-byte glyph twice
mutants.why: The lane's whole subject is stringGlyphLength against c43's extracted body; a wrong count for multi-byte glyphs is the defect it exists to catch.

mutants.what: fnPi stops lifting the stack
mutants.why: Every constant command lifts before storing; dropping the lift overwrites X instead of pushing, which the register snapshot must see.

mutants.what: uniformL answers one below the low bound
mutants.why: The lane drives uniformL-below explicitly. The earlier mutant (a zero-width range in uniformP) SURVIVED because every uniform case seeds a non-degenerate low/high pair -- a real gap, not an equivalent mutant, and the degenerate range is still unchecked.

mutants.what: dropNoise rounds at a fixed 39 digits instead of the requested precision
mutants.replace:
var c: realContext_t = runtime.ctxtReal39;
    c.round = runtime.DEC_ROUND_HALF_UP;
mutants.why: This lane drives the closed-form 2x2/3x3 workers, isRealSymmetric, dropNoise and the Householder QR step -- NOT calculateEigenvalues, the iterative driver. A mutant in that driver's convergence tolerance SURVIVED, which is how the lane's real scope became visible.

mutants.what: determineItem decodes the key index in base 11
mutants.why: The lane's subject is key-to-item dispatch through btnClicked, and this is the decode every case depends on. The earlier mutant (dropping KEY_fg from checkKeyShifts) SURVIVED: the entry corpus drives digits, ENTER and +, and no key it presses carries KEY_fg as its primary.

mutants.what: checkKeyShifts reads the standard layout while USER mode is on
mutants.find: const primary = if (use_usr) runtime.kbd_usr[key_no].primary else runtime.kbdStdAt(key_no).primary;
mutants.why: USER-mode remapping is the branch most likely to be dropped in a port, and both keyboard lanes drive it.

mutants.what: atan skips its 1/x range reduction
mutants.why: Every case in this lane runs at ctxtReal39, so the 1071-digit selector is unreachable from it and a mutant there SURVIVED as an equivalent. This one is on the 39-digit path the lane actually drives. NOTE: no lane in this tree drives the 1071-digit atan or atan2 implementations at all.

mutants.what: atan2 loses the sign of a negative y
mutants.find:
const xNeg = realIsNegative(x);
    const yNeg = realIsNegative(y);
mutants.replace:
const xNeg = realIsNegative(x);
    const yNeg = false;
mutants.why: Same reason as math_atan: the lane drives ctxtReal39 only, so the precision selector is not reachable. Quadrant handling is what atan2 is for and this lane sweeps the sign combinations.

mutants.what: the Taylor kernel drops to 51 digits where it should use 75
mutants.why: The working precision of the sin/cos/tan Taylor series is what these oracles measure to the last digit.

mutants.what: asin accepts an argument above one instead of answering NaN
mutants.why: Kept because the reason is worth more than the entry. This lane drives Asin/Acos/SinhCosh/Tanh/ArcSinh/ArcTanh, not the circular Taylor kernel -- a mutant in that kernel SURVIVED because at 39 digits its branch is never taken. The killing mutant for this lane is the asin arithmetic below.
mutants.expected_survivor: EQUIVALENT, not a gap. The corpus does drive asin at 2 and -2, but the guard is only an early-out: without it, 1-x*x is negative, realSquareRoot answers NaN and the whole expression is NaN anyway. Both sides agree either way.

mutants.what: a NaN component stops poisoning both outputs
mutants.why: or -> and: one NaN component now falls through to the arithmetic instead of short-circuiting, which is exactly the kind of edit a port makes by accident.

mutants.what: PCG32 stops advancing its state
mutants.replace:
const step = abi.pcg32.random(rng.state, rng.inc);
    return step.value;
mutants.why: A generator that does not advance returns the same number forever, and a lane comparing a sequence against c43's must notice from the second draw.

mutants.what: a refused load leaves the previous load's temporaryInformation standing
mutants.find: runtime.temporaryInformation = runtime.TI_NO_INFO; // only a completed load sets TI_PROGRAM_LOADED, so a refusal cannot leave the previous load's value standing.
mutants.why: The clear is the port's own fix for a stale-status defect, and the lane cannot see it removed. Recorded rather than widened; the killing mutant for this lane is the load bound below.
mutants.expected_survivor: A GAP, not an equivalence. temporaryInformation IS in the compared snapshot, but the fixture resets it to 0 before every case, so a refused load leaves 0 whether or not the owner clears it. Reaching this needs a case that seeds TI_PROGRAM_LOADED and then refuses -- the same shape as the SPCRES precondition in the full-core lane.

mutants.what: asin's half-angle identity adds where it subtracts
mutants.why: angle = 2*atan(x/(1+sqrt(1-x*x))). The lane drives asin at 0, +-0.5 and +-1, so a sign error in the radicand moves every in-domain answer.

mutants.what: the load path drops its 16-bit program-size bound
mutants.why: freeProgramBytes is a uint16_t and addSpaceAfterPrograms takes a uint16_t, so a larger claim reserves only its low 16 bits while the read loop writes them all. The lane drives oversized loads.
